correctness.rationale: A cubical product cell in the Stirling complex has at least one stationary coordinate at every tree vertex; any nontrivial graph automorphism moving some vertex therefore fixes no cell and no point. This proves rational cellular chain modules are free Q[G]-modules with multiplicity the number of G-cell orbits. Kozlov Theorem 2.1 gives the single possible reduced degree d=n-m and sphere count f(m,n). Equivariant Euler–Poincaré after subtracting the trivial augmentation yields q·Q[G]+(-1)^(d+1)·1, and semisimplicity converts the virtual character into actual representations. Positivity of trivial and nontrivial multiplicities forces q>=0 and q>=1 in even degree, including trivial-G boundary separately. For n=m the complex has m! isolated points, consistent with reduced degree zero. The free action and simply connected wedge for d>=2 give the quotient fundamental group; exact rational coinvariants yield its homology. Small examples and divisibility are independently confirmed algebraically, while the all-tree theorem uses cellular freeness and the published wedge theorem, not finite tests.
residual_risks: Rational representation and rational quotient homology only; integral G-lattice or quotient torsion is not determined.
